clusters.name: Secondary school and stepfamily strain, 1987
clusters.reason: Around the time you began secondary school, your stepfather was away (your parents separated briefly over having a baby), and you made the chess squad but felt out of your depth. Your relationship with your stepfather stayed distant while you sought your dad's notice, and anxiety rose around the competition.

clusters.name: Conservatory crisis and family losses, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Your grandfather died in June 1991 and your grandmother had surgery for a thyroid tumour around the same time. Your wrist injury in the first term at Wexley stopped your playing and brought a blow-up with Rafe. You dropped out, spent a bleak year at community college, then found your footing again with the Lisbon exchange. Throughout, you had late nights and slept poorly, your mother filled in your college forms while you underfunctioned, and you were anxious about your dad not knowing your film. The losses and your injury piled up while you were away from home for the first time.

clusters.name: Performance peak and split from Joelle, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: You were playing the best you ever had and winning competitions, but insomnia began getting in the way before performances. Within months you separated from Joelle, and you started therapy after the split to think through family patterns.

clusters.name: Burnout and depression after Marisol, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: You ran out of steam for performing from 2001 onward, felt on poor terms with family and friends, and were distance from your parents. Your grandmother was found to have bowel cancer and spent her final months in your parents' home. You left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, met Marisol, moved to Fenwick with her, then split within the year and sank into a deep depression once back in Thornbury. Your anxiety rose about facing your family, but you leaned on friends like Corbin and Hamish. Your dad and Corbin spoke several times, and by January 2004 you were back with your therapist and began swimming. Your grandmother died in February. What shifted was that you asked your parents for help with therapy costs and began to recover.

clusters.name: Cutoff from mother at nursing school, 2008
clusters.reason: Your grandmother Lorna died in January 2008, and your grandfather Clifford died that same year. You spent four weeks building at Alder Creek with Silas that summer, but were too drained for conversation with your mother. She pressed you to visit, you kept the door shut on her, and when you left for nursing school in Marlow Sound in September you stopped speaking to her—a silence that held for roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke and began showing memory loss around the same time. The cutoff eased once you were settled and could keep up mature ties, though you felt distant from both parents through the lodge visit.

clusters.name: Marriage and strain with Wren's family, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: You married Wren in March 2017 and saw your mother a bit less once she came along. Your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in late 2017. Your sister Tara married in 2018 and was expecting a baby by October 2019. Around the same time, Wren's brother Leo returned to live nearby with his family. In October 2019 Wren was swamped with events, and you overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her. You noticed she talks with her father and brother all day in a fused way. At her mother's retirement party at the lake house that same weekend, you couldn't sleep from the small hours onward and felt you didn't belong with her family. Your anxiety about sleep worsened around her family occasions, though your job had steadied and paid well. The events show your own anxiety rising, your sleep at its worst around her relatives, and strain in how you and Wren manage her family's closeness.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
